run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:42:48Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by 504 Gateway Timeouts on the /api/recommendations route: Envoy in frontend-proxy aborted upstream requests after 15000 ms ('504 UT response_timeout'), and frontend-proxy ingress error rate rose from a sporadic 0.0111/s background to 0.0667/s at 01:43:48 and 0.1667/s at 01:45:48, then fell back to 0 by 01:50:48. The timed-out upstream is the recommendation service: frontend's client span to grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations took 15.07 s in a sampled trace, and among ~364 such client spans in the 6 minutes ending 01:50:00, 48 exceeded 15 s and only ~29 completed within 1 s, versus all ~347 spans within 1 s in the 6 minutes ending 01:36:00. The only fault-injection evidence in the window is chaos-mesh CPU stress: the Schedule otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress (namespace chaos-mesh) spawned StressChaos experiments every minute from 01:39:44 to 01:47:44 whose 'Applied' messages name 'otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv/recommendation'. recommendation's pod stayed Running/Ready with 0 restarts, its logs show it kept receiving ListRecommendations calls, and product-catalog (its dependency) stayed at ~1.9 ms p95 — so the supported reading is that CPU stress starved recommendation until frontend-proxy's 15 s timeout fired, but the chaos objects themselves could not be read, so the cause rests on events and the finding is partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress spans recorded STATUS_CODE_ERROR at a sporadic ~0.0111/s from about 01:26:48, rose to 0.06666666666666665/s at the 01:43:48 sample and 0.16666666666666666/s at 01:45:48, then read 0 at 01:50:48 and 01:52:48 (rate over [2m], 60 s steps, span_name="ingress").

Every one of the 40 frontend-proxy ingress ERROR spans in the retained sample carries http.status_code=504 and otel.status_code=ERROR with duration about 15,000,000 us (15 s), each matched by a 'router frontend egress' span of the same ~15 s duration with http.status_code "0", i.e. the proxy gave up waiting for the upstream.

frontend-proxy container logs record 'GET /api/recommendations?productIds=... HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout' with a 15000 ms upstream time; 46 such lines were matched between 2026-11-18T01:44:26.590Z and 2026-11-18T01:48:12.168Z.

In trace 40fc89a0cadcbbb31ce5939d98b85f7e, frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations lasted 15,074,102 us and the whole /api/recommendations request 15,077,075 us, while frontend's four ProductCatalogService/GetProduct client spans took 1,544-2,053 us and product-catalog's four server spans 38-147 us; frontend returned http.status_code 200 for the route while frontend-proxy recorded the ingress as 504.

Latency to recommendation rose sharply: for the 6 minutes ending 01:36:00 essentially all frontend client spans to grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations were within 1000 ms (346.9 in the le=1000 ms bucket of 346.9 at +Inf), whereas for the 6 minutes ending 01:50:00 there were 364.4 spans in +Inf, only 29.5 within 1000 ms, 267.3 within 10,000 ms, 316.4 within 15,000 ms and 48.1 above 15,000 ms.

Chaos-mesh events record nine StressChaos experiments started at 01:39:44, 01:40:44, 01:41:44, 01:42:44, 01:43:44, 01:44:44, 01:45:44, 01:46:44 and 01:47:44 whose Applied message is 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv/recommendation', each followed about 55 s later by 'Time up according to the duration' and a 'Successfully recover chaos' message.

The chaos-mesh object Schedule otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress (namespace chaos-mesh) emitted 'Create new object: otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress-<suffix>' Spawned events every minute from 01:39:44 to 01:47:44, so it is the object that produced the StressChaos experiments applied to the recommendation pod.

Pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, and its container log shows repeated 'Receive ListRecommendations for product ids:[...]' lines up to 2026-11-18T01:47:52.852Z, so it continued to accept work during the stress rather than crashing.

recommendation's own span counters show /oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations, /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts and get_product_list at 70.66666666666666 spans in the 2 minutes ending 01:40:48 and 0 in every 2-minute sample from 01:42:48 through 01:52:48, and its ListRecommendations duration histogram had no increase over the 6 minutes ending 01:50:00 (all buckets 0).

In the 10 minutes ending 01:52:00 the only error-status spans were frontend-proxy ingress (60.526927777777786) plus flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream errors on fraud-detection (1.061875925925926) and ad (1.061875925925926); every frontend span operation (GET, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, grpc clients, executing api route, tcp.connect) reported 0 error spans, as did cart, payment, ad and the other listed services.

product-catalog's oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts server-span p95 latency was 1.9287878787878785 ms for the 6 minutes ending 01:50:00, so recommendation's dependency was fast while recommendation was timing out.

The 5xx responses in frontend-proxy logs before the 504 burst were five 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' responses on /api/products and /api/cart between 01:21:01.005Z and 01:36:10.440Z - a different, earlier and lower-rate error mode than the 504 response_timeout burst on /api/recommendations.

All 12 flags in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) have defaultVariant "off", including recommendationCacheFailure, adHighCpu, kafkaQueueProblems and emailMemoryLeak, so no flag-based fault injection for recommendation is visible in that ConfigMap's current content.
Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-dz8j9 shows restartCount 3 with lastState terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-18T01:22:23Z, which is before the alert start of 01:42:48Z.

Mechanism hypothesis: repeated CPU stress on the single recommendation pod (container 'recommendation') starved the process so ListRecommendations calls took over 15 s, exceeding frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream response timeout, which produced the 504 UT response_timeout responses and the frontend-proxy ingress error rate the alert reports; the burst timing (01:43:48-01:48:48 elevated, back to 0 after the last StressChaos recovered) matches the chaos cycles, but no CPU metric was available to measure the starvation directly.

Unresolved sub-hypothesis: recommendation's span counters and duration histogram going to zero after about 01:41:48 may mean span export stalled under the CPU starvation rather than that recommendation stopped handling requests, since its container log keeps showing incoming ListRecommendations calls during the same period; server-side latency inside recommendation could not be read directly.

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running and Ready at query time and recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv had restartCount 0, so the timeout burst is not explained by a crashed, restarting or evicted recommendation pod.

No flag in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config is switched on (all defaultVariant "off", including recommendationCacheFailure), so the evidence does not show a feature-flag fault injection behind the recommendation slowness.

recommendation's downstream product-catalog was fast during the burst (ListProducts p95 1.9287878787878785 ms for the 6 minutes ending 01:50:00, and 38-147 us server spans in trace 40fc89a0cadcbbb31ce5939d98b85f7e), so the latency does not originate in that dependency.

Rejected as the cause of this alert: the fraud-detection container OOMKilled restarts (3 restarts, last termination exitCode 137 at 01:22:23Z) - they finished about 20 minutes before the alert start of 01:42:48Z, the alert-time burst consists of 504 response_timeout on /api/recommendations, and fraud-detection shows only its background flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream error spans (1.06 in the 10 minutes to 01:52:00).

Have the chaos-mesh owner review and stop/pause the Schedule otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress in namespace chaos-mesh (or its spawned StressChaos experiments) before any further mitigation, and confirm whether CPU stress on recommendation was intended for this window.

After the chaos is removed, consider adding recommendation replicas and explicit CPU requests/limits so a single stressed pod cannot exhaust the service, and add alerting on recommendation-side p95 latency and on per-route frontend-proxy 5xx (the 504s are Envoy's 15 s upstream response_timeout) so the timeout route is visible earlier than a service-wide error-rate alert.

gaps: The chaos-mesh Schedule and StressChaos objects could not be read (their kinds are not in the permitted Kubernetes resource list), so the CPU load/worker values, the duration and mode settings, whether the Schedule is still active, and when it was created are unknown; the fault itself is known only from events.
Change history is not integrated, so what enabled the Schedule stress at 01:39:44 and whether anything else changed on recommendation at that time cannot be verified.
The alert rule RequestErrorRate was not found in the Prometheus rules (the rule query returned nothing), so the exact alert expression, threshold and lookback are unverified.

recommendation's own server-side span data was not retrievable: traces_search_by_tags for recommendation /oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations with min_duration 5s between 01:39:00 and 01:50:00 returned nothing, and its span counters read 0 after the 01:42:48 sample, so server-side latency inside recommendation during the stress is unknown rather than measured.

The frontend-proxy log read reached the 4 MiB limit at 2026-11-18T01:40:09.992Z, so 5xx lines between 01:40:09 and 01:44:26 were not read and the exact transition from the earlier 503 upstream_reset errors to the 504 response_timeout burst is unknown.

The recommendation error-filtered log query returned no_data (not citable), so absence of error lines in that pod is not established; only unfiltered 'Receive ListRecommendations ...' lines were observed.

Application logs of the other services (cart, checkout, payment, currency, shipping, email, accounting, quote, ad, image-provider, kafka, postgresql, valkey) were not read; their health is supported only by zero error-span counts and pod readiness.
Why the fraud-detection pod was OOMKilled (3 restarts, last at 01:22:23Z) was not investigated; it is recorded as a change in the window not tied to this alert.
Kubernetes objects were read after the window, so pod and ConfigMap state cannot prove the state during the incident; the flagd flags could have been different at 01:43.
